evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript with supporting citations

claim: MESA is a contiguous geographic area surrounding Marshfield, Wisconsin, where nearly all 61,000 residents receive outpatient and inpatient care from the Marshfield Clinic Health System.
source: MESA is a contiguous geographic area surrounding Marshfield, Wisconsin, where nearly all 61,000 residents receive outpatient and inpatient care from the Marshfield Clinic Health System (Kieke et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kieke et al., 2015

claim: The relative burden of cases is consistently higher in people ≥65 years old during H3N2-dominated seasons compared to H1N1-dominated seasons.
source: The relative burden of cases is consistently higher in people ≥65 years old during H3N2-dominated seasons compared to H1N1-dominated seasons (Figure 2).

claim: The risk of future medically attended infection by H3N2 is reduced by 33% (95% CI 17–46%) in people imprinted to H3N2.

evidence: Supported by model estimates with confidence intervals

claim: There is no evidence of a protective effect from imprinting to N2 (0%, 95% CI 0–7%).

claim: The best-fitting model includes age-specific risk of medically attended influenza A infection, HA subtype imprinting, and age-specific VE.

claim: The model underestimates aggregate H1N1 cases in unvaccinated 5–9 year-olds, largely driven by infection during the 2009 H1N1 pandemic.

claim: Primary infection appears to reduce the risk of medically attended infection with that subtype throughout life.

source: This effect is stronger for H1N1 compared to H3N2.
